title: Dense compactification of a proper morphism over an open preserves its finite generic fibres
statement: Let $S$ be a reduced Noetherian scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Let $u:U\hookrightarrow S$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and $z:Z\to U$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume that $uz:Z\to S$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology]. Then there are a proper morphism $b:B\to S$ and an open immersion $j:Z\hookrightarrow B$ with $bj=uz$, whose image is dense in the underlying topological space of $B$, such that the square with sides $z,j,u,b$ is Cartesian: the induced $U$-morphism $Z\to B\times_SU$ is an isomorphism [def-pc-fibre-product]. For every generic point $s$ of an irreducible component of $S$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components], the scheme $B_s=B\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field] is finite over $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; if $s\notin U$, this fibre is empty. Neither $S$ nor $Z$ is assumed integral, and $U$ and $Z$ may be empty.

source.place: Expose II Theorem 3.2.1, ordinary-case proof, printed p.29, compactification sentence; II Proposition 1.1.7 and Definition 1.2.2, printed p.24, for finite generic fibres. Compactification input: Stacks Tag 0F41, literature/stacks-project/flat.tex, theorem-nagata.

proof.text: Put $f=u\circ z$. By [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology], $f$ is of finite type, every component generic point of $Z$ maps to a component generic point of $S$, and its residue-field extension is finite. The finite affine cover in the hypothesis makes $S$ locally Noetherian by [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact: each affine is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact], and the union is finite. Thus $S$ is quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Moreover $f$ is separated. Indeed, because $u$ identifies $U$ with an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], two maps to $U$ agree if their composites to $S$ agree. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] therefore identifies $Z\times_SZ$ with $Z\times_UZ$, carrying $\Delta_f$ to $\Delta_z$. The latter is a closed immersion since $z$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Expose II Theorem 3.2.1, ordinary-case proof, printed p.29, compactification sentence; II Proposition 1.1.7 and Definition 1.2.2, printed pp.23–24.

proof.text: Apply [det-nagata-theorem-dense] to the separated finite-type map $f$ over the qcqs base $S$. Unpack [def-nagata-compactification]: it gives $Z\xrightarrow{j}B\xrightarrow{b}S$, with $j$ an open immersion, $b$ proper, $bj=f$, and an injective sheaf map $\mathcal O_B\to j_*\mathcal O_Z$. The image of $j$ is topologically dense. Otherwise its closure has a nonempty open complement $W$. On every open $A\subseteq W$ the target ring $\mathcal O_Z(j^{-1}A)$ is zero, so injectivity forces $\mathcal O_B(A)=0$. The stalk at any point of $W$ is then zero, contradicting its being a local ring of a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Finally $b$ is finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian].

source.place: Expose II Theorem 3.2.1, ordinary-case proof, printed p.29, compactification sentence; II Proposition 1.1.7 and Definition 1.2.2, printed pp.23–24.

proof.text: Identify $B_U=B\times_SU$ with the inverse-image open $b^{-1}(U)$ using [lem-weil-pbc-open-preimage-fibre-product]. The equation $bj=uz$ induces $k:Z\to B_U$; it is an open immersion because $j$ is the isomorphism onto its open image and that image lies in $b^{-1}(U)$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. The structural map $B_U\to U$ is separated by [lem-weil-pbc-separated-base-change], since $b$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. As $z$ is proper and $k$ is a $U$-morphism, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] makes $k$ proper; [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image] makes its image closed in $B_U$. Its image is dense there: every nonempty open of the open subset $b^{-1}(U)\subseteq B$ meets the dense open $j(Z)$. Consequently $k$ is a surjective open immersion, hence an isomorphism onto $B_U$ by the defining isomorphism onto the image in [def-weil-open-immersion]. This proves the required Cartesian square.

source.place: Expose II Theorem 3.2.1, ordinary-case proof, printed p.29, compactification sentence; II Proposition 1.1.7 and Definition 1.2.2, printed pp.23–24.

proof.text: The Noetherian scheme $B$ has finitely many irreducible components by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], each with a unique generic point by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. Fix a component $C$ with generic point $\xi$. Remove all the other components to get an open $W$ meeting $C$ at $\xi$. It is nonempty, so density gives $W\cap j(Z)\ne\varnothing$. This is a nonempty open of the irreducible $C$, hence contains $\xi$: otherwise the closure of $\{\xi\}=C$ would lie in its closed complement [def-sc-generic-point]. Thus every component generic point of $B$ lies in $j(Z)$. Under the open-subscheme isomorphism [def-weil-open-immersion] it is a component generic point of $Z$: any larger irreducible subset of $Z$ would have closure in $B$ strictly containing $C$, contrary to maximality [def-weil-irreducible-components]. The local rings, and hence residue fields, at the corresponding points are identical. The object condition [def-per-ordinary-alteration-topology] now gives that $b(\xi)$ is a component generic point of $S$ and $\kappa(\xi)/\kappa(b(\xi))$ is finite.

proof.text: The map $b$ is finite type, the base $S$ is Noetherian, and Step 4 verifies both maximal dominance and finite extensions at every component generic point of $B$. Apply [lem-per-generic-fibre-finiteness-criterion] with $X=B$ and $f=b$. Its final clause states exactly that $B_s$ is finite over $\kappa(s)$ for every component generic point $s$ of $S$. This applies to the whole scheme fibre, including its scheme structure; it is not merely finiteness of its set of points.

source.place: Expose II Theorem 3.2.1, ordinary-case proof, printed p.29, compactification sentence; II Proposition 1.1.7 and Definition 1.2.2, printed pp.23–24.

proof.text: Let $s$ be a component generic point of $S$ outside $U$. If $x\in B$ mapped to $s$, choose an irreducible component $C$ containing $x$ by [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover] and its generic point $\xi$ by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. Continuity gives $s\in\overline{\{b(\xi)\}}$. Step 4 says $b(\xi)$ is a component generic point. Taking closures therefore includes the component $\overline{\{s\}}$ in the component $\overline{\{b(\xi)\}}$, so maximality makes them equal [def-weil-irreducible-components]; uniqueness of generic points in $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] gives $s=b(\xi)$. But Step 4 also puts $\xi$ in $j(Z)$, whose image under $b$ lies in $U$, a contradiction. Thus no point of $B$ lies over $s$. A point of $B_s$ would project to such a point by the commuting projections [def-pc-fibre-product], so $B_s$ is empty. If $Z$ is empty, Step 2 forces $B$ empty by density; the same construction and arguments cover empty $U$ or $S$.

Step 2: dense Nagata (Stacks 0F41) gives O_B ↪ j_*O_Z, which forces topological density (a zero stalk on an open missing j(Z) contradicts locality); B is Noetherian by 01T6. Step 3: b⁻¹(U) = B_U; k is proper by proper-to-separated, so its image is closed, and it is also dense, so k is an isomorphism and the square is Cartesian. Step 4: every component generic point of B lies in the dense open j(Z) and is a component generic point of Z there, so the alt/S conditions transfer to b. Step 5: lem-per-generic-fibre-finiteness-criterion (ILO II 1.1.7, p.24) gives finite scheme fibres. Step 6: specialization, maximality and sobriety give empty fibres outside U.
